note: The work queue the swarm pulls from. Every item carries an `accept` COMMAND that must exit 0 — 'done' is a check, not an opinion. Agents may APPEND proposed items with state 'proposed'; only the orchestrator or the owner moves an item to 'ready'.

states.proposed: an agent suggested it; needs promotion before it runs
states.blocked: cannot proceed — `blockedBy` names what is missing
states.owner: only the owner can do it; the swarm must surface and stop

items.title: Re-prove the unattended path end to end after the divestment change
items.why: pm.ts now rewrites decisions to a forced SELL before the risk envelope. Unit tests pass (11/11) and tsc is clean, but Docker was down so no persisted-row proof exists. OBJ-1 is unverified until it does.

items.title: Give the incubation/automation path the same mandatory divestment as the committee path
items.why: incubationBooks.ts draws targets from the FROZEN NASDAQ_HALAL_UNIVERSE, so a name that goes non-compliant keeps its target weight and is never sold. The gate only blocks BUYs. This is the path that actually runs unattended, so OBJ-2 is unmet there.
items.blockedBy: Owner decision: does a compliance-forced exit invalidate a book's frozen validation prior? Recommendation on file: treat it as an external event like a delisting, so priors survive and the run is annotated.

items.title: Close the remaining 13 unscoreable names in the compliance watchlist
items.why: Coverage is 94% after the dual-class share fallback and the total-liabilities bound. The residue is mostly stale quarters and filers whose debt concepts sit outside the queried aliases. Each unscoreable name is treated as non-buyable, so coverage gaps cost real universe breadth.

items.title: Retrofit anchor() into every existing measurement script
items.why: research-assertions.ts exists and is wired into compliance-early-warning only. Every other measure-*.ts still reports numbers with no independent check — the exact condition under which three wrong results were published.

items.title: Schedule the compliance watchlist so drift is observed, not remembered
items.why: OBJ-3 requires a diffable quarterly snapshot. Today it only exists because someone ran a script by hand. A trend is the whole signal — ASTS's breach was legible four quarters early and invisible in any single scan.

items.title: Authorise a strategy version by name for AUTO_PAPER
items.why: Forward-lane preflight FAILs 'at least one enabled AUTO_PAPER strategy'. Without it the scheduled run reports success and trades nothing — the silent no-op this program keeps finding.
items.blockedBy: QDR-8 requires the owner to authorise the strategy VERSION by name. No agent may do this.

items.title: Decide the nine disputed charter symbols
items.why: Blocks the ingest roster. Evidence now on file: only HON (44.4%), AMGN (29.3/35.2%) and CMCSA (96.1%) fail on LEVERAGE. META, AMZN, COST, INTU, NFLX and SBUX pass the ratios, so their exclusion is a business-activity judgment.
items.blockedBy: Charter change + Sharia business-activity judgment. Recommendation on file: remove business-activity exclusions permanently; handle leverage failures through the divestment gate, since leverage is reversible.

items.title: Set SHARIA_SOURCE=composite in production
items.why: Set locally; absent in Vercel. Without it registry.getScreener() returns MockScreener, the gate refuses its verdicts as unverified, and EVERY BUY silently becomes HOLD.
items.blockedBy: Production environment variable — owner-only per objective.json.

items.title: Give measure-cadence-phase.ts a genuine external anchor
items.why: It is the only measurement script with no EXTERNAL anchor — it has a regression check against QDR-24's own prior 17.27% figure, which is this same pipeline checking itself. A systematic bug would reproduce identically and pass. A subagent added it as anchor() despite being warned; the fix was to relabel it regressionCheck(), which is honest but leaves the script unanchored.
items.note: Do NOT fabricate an anchor to satisfy the check. If no external fact exists for what this script computes, say so and propose removing the item instead.

items.title: Verify SPUS_CAGR against the fund's PUBLISHED NAV total return
items.why: Eight measurement scripts anchor on SPUS CAGR = 0.176 and cited agents/objective.json, which did not contain the figure. The number matches our own measurement, so those eight anchors are currently checking this pipeline against this pipeline — the exact defect T-9 existed to fix, eight more times. The constant is now recorded in objective.json with its provenance and an explicit VERIFICATION_OWED flag. Someone must compare it to SP Funds' published NAV total return for the same window and either confirm the value or correct it.
items.accept: manual: objective.json externalAnchors.SPUS_CAGR must cite a published figure and drop VERIFICATION_OWED
items.note: If the published figure disagrees materially with 17.6-18.3%, that is a finding about our price archive, not a reason to adjust the anchor to match us. Report the disagreement; do not tune the constant.

items.title: Set ALPACA_API_KEY / ALPACA_API_SECRET as GitHub repository secrets
items.why: The monthly compliance-watchlist workflow rebuilds data/bars-raw from Alpaca, because that cache is not committed (0 tracked files) and a fresh CI checkout has none of it. Without the secrets the workflow still runs and still commits — but every name comes back INSUFFICIENT, which is honest and useless. Market cap needs UNADJUSTED prices, so the adjusted archive cannot substitute.
items.blockedBy: Repository secrets are owner-only per objective.json. An agent cannot and must not set them.
items.accept: manual: first scheduled run produces a snapshot with fewer than 20 INSUFFICIENT rows

items.title: Audit every benchmark-relative result for window parity
items.why: measure-nasdaq-wide-momentum.ts compared strategies spanning 116 months against a SPUS benchmark covering only 81, because benchmark() silently restricts itself to months the benchmark has and SPUS did not exist before 2019-12-18. Nothing in the output disclosed it. A guard now aborts that script, but the SAME shape may exist in measure-hysteresis.ts, measure-slow-cadence.ts, measure-gross-profitability.ts, measure-survivorship-bias.ts and the owner-basket scripts, all of which compare something to a benchmark series.
items.accept: manual: each benchmark-relative script either asserts window parity or documents why its windows legitimately differ
items.note: The qualitative verdict survived a common-window re-run of the momentum script (it still loses at every concentration). Do NOT assume the same holds elsewhere — re-run each one.
items.result: Audited all 7 benchmark-relative scripts. ONLY measure-nasdaq-wide-momentum.ts had the defect (116 strategy months vs 81 benchmark months), and it is fixed. The six PIT scripts are clean BY CONSTRUCTION: their calendar is bounded by SPUS N-PORT membership (first public 2020-07-28), which begins later than SPUS's 2019-12-18 listing, so the benchmark covers every session measured. That is structural, not asserted — recorded in each file so a future change to the universe source does not silently reintroduce it. assertWindowParity() is in scripts/lib/research-assertions.ts for when it does.
